text:
Noah: flagging an odd pattern: several tenants had sudden billing spikes on /v2/complete but traces show clients calling without `x-redwood-version`.
Noah: dashboard link: https://dash.internal/route/tokens?span=3h
Elena: are we still defaulting to prefer-latest when header missing? I thought we switched that to prefer-stable for safety.
Ravi: we have two deciders: (1) runtime policy prefers latest by capacity, (2) fallback rule prefers stable unless tenant has historical v2 affinity. combination can be surprising.
Noah: simplest mitigation: route unknown-version to lower-cost variant by default for 48h, and lift after RFC.
sre-bot: suggested action: toggle `unknown_version_default=lower_cost` on canary in 1m
Elena: also we lack clear telemetry: we can't attribute tokens to "declared v1 but routed v2" easily. need a metric like `tokens_by_declared_vs_routed`
Ravi: I can add a lightweight counter: increment(tag=(tenant,declared, routed_variant, seqlen_bucket)). small payload.
Billing: recommend auto-block billing escalation for tenants that see >2x bump and alert them before charging. Ops to confirm thresholds.
Noah: add a small server response header so clients can self-detect: `X-Redwood-Routed-Version: v2 (inferred)` or `v1 (declared)`. low risk and helpful.
Elena: agree. Also let's add a console CTA on route pages: "Requests without API version were routed by inference. Click to learn how to opt-in to stable routing"
Ravi: owners: canary flag flip 1m -> Noah; telemetry counter -> Ravi; console CTA -> Elena; billing safeguard -> Billing + Noah.
Noah: flipping flag on canary now. will monitor 15m.
Noah: done. canary tokens down ~40% on affected shards. :thumbsup:
Ravi: starting ingest for the new counter; will drop samples into the metrics cluster in ~8m.
Billing: we'll prepare a customer-friendly credit & outreach template and post to #customer-comms for review.
Elena: follow-ups: RFC for long-term default semantics (Elena+Ravi), and a postmortem doc pinned to the incident board.
Noah: thanks all, keeping this thread as canonical incident notes.
